G21006:

I. to have gone before, be the first, Thuc., Xen.
2. to have advanced, πρ. ἐς βαθὺ τῆς ἡλικίας Ar.; εἰς τοῦτο προήκειν to have come to this pass, Dem.; of Time, τῆς ἡμέρας προηκούσας Plut.

G21066:
πρύτανις [prob. from πρό]
I. a prince, ruler, lord, chief, of Hiero, Pind.; of Zeus, id., Aesch.
II. at Athens, a Prytanis or President: the πρυτάνεις were a committee of 50, chosen by lot from each of the 10 φυλαί, so that each set formed 1/10 part of the βουλή or Council of 500; out of these 50 πρυτάνεις one was chosen by lot as chief-president (ἐπιστάτης); he chose 9 πρόεδροι; and the real business was in the hands of this smaller body, with a secretary (γραμματεύς) added.—The φυλή which first entered office every year was determined by lot; and their term of office (πρυτανεία) was about five weeks. During this time all treaties and public acts ran in their name, in this form: Ἀκαμαντὶς [φυλὴ] ἐπρυτάνευε, Φαίνιππος ἐγραμμάτευε, Νικιάδης ἐπεστάτει the Tribe Acamantis were the Presidency, Phaenippus the Secretary, Niciades the Chief-president, Thuc.
G21067:
πρωιζός πρωιζός, αττιξ πρῳζός, όν [= πρώϊος]
I. neut. pl. πρωιζά was used as adv., just like πρώην, χθιζά τε καὶ πρωιζά yesterday or the day before, Il.
II. οὕτω δὴ πρ. κατέδραθες so very early, Theocr.

G21091:
σηκός σηκός, δοριξ σα—κός, οῦ, ὁ,

2. a sepulchre, burial-place, Simon.
III. the trunk of an old olive-tree, Lys.
G21093:
σθένω σθένω, [only in pres. and imperf.] [σθένος]
1. to have strength or might, be strong or mighty, Soph., Eur.; σθ. χερί, ποσί to be strong in hand, in foot, Soph., Eur.; σθένοντος ἐν πλούτῳ Soph.; τοσοῦτον σθένει id.; ὅσονπερ ἂν σθένῃ id.; οἱ κάτω σθένοντες they who have power below, Eur.
2. c. inf. to have strength or power to do, be able, Soph., Eur.
